caption: Collision Verlet (Houndonougbo, Laird & Leimkuhler 2000) as implemented. (a) The +/− Coulomb pair potential φc = −l_B/r (l_B = 5 σ) is split into a long-range part φ₂ that follows the Hermite cubic P(r) on [q₁, q₂] = [1, 1.5] σ and is flat at P(q₁) = −3.70 kT inside q₁, and a short-range part φ₁ = φc − φ₂ that vanishes beyond q₂; the hard core r < σ is shaded. (b) The corresponding pair forces: F₂ and its slope vanish at contact, F₁ carries the full contact force −5 kT/σ and goes to zero continuously at q₂. (c) One step h: outer half-kicks with F₂, exact hard-sphere propagation in between in which every hard collision (anywhere in the system) cuts the step into velocity-Verlet sub-steps with F₁; accelerated ions follow parabolic paths and their collision times are the smallest positive root of the quartic |Δq + Δvτ + ½Δaτ²|² = σ². The shipped cv-phys variant reflects the physical velocity v + F₂(τᵢ − h/2) at each collision instead of the drift velocity.
